translations.help.title: Help center
translations.help.description: Learn the main CodexSwitch workflows and safety boundaries, from first connection to advanced routing.
translations.help.quickStart.title: Start in four steps
translations.help.quickStart.description: Get one working connection first, then tune routing, pricing, and network settings.
translations.help.quickStart.step1.title: Add a provider
translations.help.quickStart.step1.body: Select Add provider in the lower-left corner, then choose a built-in template or create a custom provider.
translations.help.quickStart.step2.title: Enter credentials
translations.help.quickStart.step2.body: Enter an API key. For Codex OAuth, follow the login flow or import an auth JSON file.
translations.help.quickStart.step3.title: Activate it and start the proxy
translations.help.quickStart.step3.body: Set the provider as current and confirm that the proxy status on Home is running.
translations.help.quickStart.step4.title: Send a request and inspect logs
translations.help.quickStart.step4.body: Codex connects to http://127.0.0.1:12785/v1 by default. After one request, check Logs for the model, duration, and usage.
translations.help.features.title: Feature map
translations.help.features.description: The sidebar groups configuration, monitoring, and system tools.
translations.help.features.providers.title: Providers
translations.help.features.providers.body: Manage upstream URLs, credentials, protocols, default models, enabled state, and order.
translations.help.features.models.title: Models
translations.help.features.models.body: Maintain model aliases, display metadata, and local pricing for routing and cost estimates.
translations.help.features.usage.title: Home and logs
translations.help.features.usage.body: Review proxy health, request trends, tokens, cost, latency, and failures.
translations.help.features.sessions.title: Codex sessions
translations.help.features.sessions.body: See each session's provider and migrate or restore both session files and the local index after switching providers. Any failed step stops and rolls back the operation.
translations.help.features.settings.title: Settings
translations.help.features.settings.body: Switch language and theme, configure startup behavior, and inspect the local paths managed by CodexSwitch.
translations.help.providerGuide.title: Providers and Sync to Codex
translations.help.providerGuide.description: Saving, activating, and syncing a provider affect different scopes. Knowing the difference prevents the proxy from switching while Codex still shows an old model or context limit.
translations.help.providerGuide.rule.title: Quick rule
translations.help.providerGuide.rule.body: Changes used only for upstream forwarding usually need Save. Changes to Codex startup configuration, the model catalog, or context capabilities should be followed by Sync to Codex.
translations.help.providerGuide.sync.title: Sync in these cases
translations.help.providerGuide.sync.item1: • The first time Codex uses a provider, or after Manage Codex config was disabled. Sync enables management and makes the provider current.
translations.help.providerGuide.sync.item2: • Switching to a Codex provider with a different default model or model list. Activate the card first, then sync so Codex reloads the catalog.
translations.help.providerGuide.sync.item3: • Changing 1M context, the default model, model routes or display names, service tier, or fast mode. These values are written to config.toml or the model catalog.
translations.help.providerGuide.sync.item4: • Changing Codex support or WebSocket support, or when Codex still shows old settings. Sync rewrites configuration and attempts to restart Codex.
translations.help.providerGuide.save.title: Changes that usually only need Save
translations.help.providerGuide.save.item1: • Base URL, API key, upstream protocol, upstream model, and model conversions are read by the local proxy. Saving the active provider reloads proxy routing.
translations.help.providerGuide.save.item2: • Usage queries and billing multipliers mainly affect quota checks, statistics, and cost estimates, so Codex does not need to reload.
translations.help.providerGuide.save.item3: • Editing an inactive provider stores the configuration first; it joins routing after activation. If its catalog or context also changed, sync after activation.
translations.help.providerGuide.types.title: Switching provider types
translations.help.providerGuide.types.item1: • The Codex / Claude Code selector switches client views. A provider appears according to its Supports Codex and Supports Claude Code options.
translations.help.providerGuide.types.item2: • Responses, Chat, and Anthropic are upstream protocols. Codex always calls the local Responses endpoint and CodexSwitch performs conversion.
translations.help.providerGuide.types.item3: • Sync to Codex is shown only for Codex providers. For Claude Code, save its page settings and enable managed Claude Code configuration in Settings.
translations.help.providerGuide.flow.title: What Sync to Codex does
translations.help.providerGuide.flow.step1: Fully stops Codex and safely migrates session files and index entries from old providers such as custom to meteor-ai
translations.help.providerGuide.flow.step2: Makes the selected provider current and enables Manage Codex config
translations.help.providerGuide.flow.step3: Writes config.toml, auth, and the model catalog
translations.help.providerGuide.flow.step5: Reopens Codex with the new settings and migrated sessions
translations.help.providerGuide.verify.title: How to confirm it loaded
translations.help.providerGuide.verify.body: Check the status message at the top. If old sessions cannot be migrated safely, sync is cancelled before configuration is rewritten, preventing a partial file/index migration. Sync requires an enabled provider and a running local proxy.
translations.help.advanced.title: Advanced configuration
translations.help.advanced.description: Adjust these options only after the basic request path is stable.
translations.help.advanced.routing.title: Protocols and model routing
translations.help.advanced.routing.body: Choose Responses, Chat, or Anthropic for the upstream and configure model conversion, service tier, and fast mode.
translations.help.advanced.network.title: Local and outbound network
translations.help.advanced.network.body: Set the listen address, port, system or custom proxy, HTTP version, and connection timeout.
translations.help.advanced.auth.title: Authentication and client config
translations.help.advanced.auth.body: Protect the local inbound API and choose whether to manage Codex or Claude Code config or preserve Codex App sign-in.
translations.help.advanced.pricing.title: Pricing and multipliers
translations.help.advanced.pricing.body: Maintain billing units, model prices, and provider multipliers. Displayed costs are local estimates, not provider invoices.
translations.help.notes.title: Before changing managed configuration
translations.help.notes.body: Managed mode writes ~/.codex/config.toml, auth.json, or ~/.claude/settings.json and uses matching .bak files for backup and restore. Treat API keys, OAuth tokens, and backups as sensitive. Keep the listen address at 127.0.0.1 unless LAN access is explicitly required.
translations.help.troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
translations.help.troubleshooting.description: Check status, request details, then configuration to isolate most problems quickly.
translations.help.troubleshooting.proxy.title: The proxy will not start
translations.help.troubleshooting.proxy.body: Check the Home status and message, confirm the port is free, and verify Host and Port in Settings.
translations.help.troubleshooting.request.title: Requests fail or use the wrong model
translations.help.troubleshooting.request.body: Check the log status code, then verify Base URL, API key, protocol, default model, and model conversion rules.
translations.help.troubleshooting.config.title: The client still uses old settings
translations.help.troubleshooting.config.body: Confirm the proxy is enabled and apply the configuration again. Fully quit and restart Codex or Claude Code if needed.
